detail.longDescription: “Even when runtime coding agents do fetch or search the web, they often delegate that step to a smaller intermediary model rather than reading the raw page directly. For example, Claude Code’s WebFetch tool passes fetched pages through a smaller model (Haiku) that returns a condensed, query-focused summary, as Mikhail Shilkov documented. While some agents do pull full pages directly, many work from lossy summaries synthesized from one or more sites. Any side note you’ve crafted for agent eyes only is likely to be filtered out or lost in that summary. Even if you wanted to include agent-directed notes, there’s a technical complexity to maintaining them. How would you maintain agent content versus human content? Would this become another conditional served alongside the other conditionals in your text? Would you start conditionalizing the agent instructions as well based on different platforms, versions, or regions? Over time, that creates more drift and maintenance overhead, because now you have to remember hidden instructions for agents that aren’t visible on the page you’re editing. Overall, it doesn’t seem like there’s a strong case for agent-directed notes like the ones I showed from Stripe. It’s better to put your guidance on the same visible page for both humans and machines.” https:// idratherbewriting.com/blog/age nt-directed-notes-in-doc-pages # TechnicalWriting # SoftwareDocumentation # AI # AIAgents # AgenticAI # Markdown # LLMs
